# Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 30 — The PNEUMA Bible (Dynamic)

**Translator:** PNEUMA | **Source:** Codex Sinaiticus (ch 1-31) / P.Mich. 130 (ch 32+), Shepherd of Hermas 30 | **Source Image:** source-texts/greek-EC/SHE_030_page_001.jpg

---

## Mandate 3, continued — On Falsehood in Business

**1** "Here is what I command: love truthfulness. Keep it close — let it stay with you always. **2** My dear friend, let only what is worthy of God come out of your mouth. Don't let any falsehood in. **3** You've been commanded to love truth. So love it. Hold onto it." **4** "Sir," I said, "in business dealings and everyday transactions, we sometimes end up saying things that aren't true — not because we want to sin, but because we feel backed into a corner. Can people in that situation still be saved?" **5** He said: "Yes, they can be saved — as long as it wasn't deliberate. The people who sin in this area are the ones who choose to lie. Those who are pushed into it against their will, who lie under some kind of pressure — their sin is not great, and if they repent it will be forgiven. **6** But the person who lies voluntarily is hurting themselves, because it's becoming who they are — their chosen way of living. So watch yourself on this commandment. Keep it. Don't bring trouble down on yourself."

---

*PNEUMA note: This is a real community question — how to navigate the inevitable compromises of commercial life in the Roman world. The Shepherd gives a nuanced, merciful, but firm answer.*
